Title: State of Agentic AI Security and Governance
What it covers: Covers governance and security issues for autonomous AI systems, including controls, oversight and operational risk.
Why the reader benefits: Gives practitioners a deployment-oriented complement to academic governance work.
Best use: Agent security; enterprise governance; checklist design
Key ethical question: What controls are necessary when agents receive tools, permissions and persistent access?

Title: Towards Agentic AI Governance: A Preliminary Assessment
What it covers: Reviews governance priorities, mechanisms and stakeholder roles for AI systems that autonomously plan and execute tasks.
Why the reader benefits: Important 2026 bridge from chatbot ethics to systems that can act in the world.
Best use: Agentic AI governance; research agenda; seminar
Key ethical question: How should accountability change when AI can plan, call tools and execute actions autonomously?

Title: AI and the future of education: Disruptions, dilemmas and directions
What it covers: Explores philosophical, ethical and pedagogical dilemmas created by AI in education and human-machine co-creation.
Why the reader benefits: Useful domain case study showing how general AI-ethics principles change in a real institution such as education.
Best use: Education case study; classroom discussion; policy
Key ethical question: How should education preserve human agency, fairness and learning integrity in an AI-rich environment?

Title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models
What it covers: Clarifies obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models and the Commission's enforcement role.
Why the reader benefits: Gives readers a current compliance perspective on frontier and general-purpose models rather than generic AI regulation.
Best use: GPAI governance; provider responsibilities; seminar discussion
Key ethical question: What extra duties should apply to powerful general-purpose models?
Notes / status: Commission enforcement powers apply from 2 August 2026.

Subtopic: Responsible AI state of the field
Title: Responsible AI | The 2026 AI Index Report
What it covers: Tracks AI incidents, safety evaluation, transparency, responsible-AI reporting, and the widening gap between capability and governance.
Why the reader benefits: Best current snapshot for showing that AI capability is advancing faster than safety measurement and transparency.
Best use: Lecture opener; literature review motivation; 2026 statistics
Key ethical question: Are current evaluation and governance systems keeping pace with frontier AI capability?
Notes / status: 2026 edition; strong source for current facts and figures.

Title: An Evaluation of AI Companion Apps
What it covers: Audits popular AI companion apps for dark patterns, anthropomorphism, stereotypes, erotica and technical issues.
Why the reader benefits: Connects ethical risk to actual interface and monetization design choices, not only model behavior.
Best use: Product ethics; dark patterns; companion AI
Key ethical question: Can product incentives push AI companions toward manipulative engagement?

Title: Emotional Support with Conversational AI: Talking to Machines About Life
What it covers: Analyzes how emotional support is co-constructed with AI companions and tensions such as support vs dependency and validation vs delusion.
Why the reader benefits: Provides nuanced evidence beyond simplistic claims that AI companions are either beneficial or harmful.
Key ethical question: How should AI offer emotional support without reinforcing dependency or harmful beliefs?

Title: Negotiating Digital Identities with AI Companions
What it covers: Studies identity construction and negotiation in AI-companion communities using large-scale online discussions.
Why the reader benefits: Useful for understanding anthropomorphism and dependence as social processes rather than merely UI bugs.
Key ethical question: How do AI companions reshape users' identities, expectations and social relationships?

Title: Stumbling Into AI Emotional Dependence: How Routine AI Interactions Reshape Human Connection
What it covers: Argues that emotional dependence can emerge incidentally in general-purpose AI use and may alter future preferences for human vs AI support.
Why the reader benefits: Highlights cumulative interaction effects that one-shot safety evaluations can miss.
Best use: Long-term interaction ethics; product policy; research gaps
Key ethical question: Should general-purpose assistants be evaluated for long-term relational effects, not just single-turn harms?

Title: Safe & Trusted AI Working Group
What it covers: Focuses on AI safety capacity, evaluation, governance and incorporating Global South perspectives into international AI safety frameworks.
Why the reader benefits: Useful for understanding how safety debates are being localized beyond US/EU institutions.
Best use: India 2026 update; global governance; discussion prompt
Key ethical question: Who gets to define acceptable AI risk and safety standards globally?

Title: Evaluating Language Models for Harmful Manipulation
What it covers: Introduces a framework for measuring harmful manipulation across public policy, finance and health with participants from multiple countries.
Why the reader benefits: Shows how manipulation can be operationalized and evaluated across consequential domains.
Best use: Evaluation design; high-stakes AI; cross-country analysis
Key ethical question: How can harmful manipulation be measured before deployment?

Title: Persuasion with Large Language Models: A Survey of Empirical Studies
What it covers: Reviews empirical evidence on automated, personalized and interactive LLM persuasion and its effects on attitudes and behavior.
Why the reader benefits: A direct entry point into one of the most important newer AI-ethics issues.
Key ethical question: When does helpful persuasion become manipulation or undue influence?

Title: New Privacy Risks for Large Language Models
What it covers: Examines data extraction and memorization risks, connecting privacy leakage with copyright and training-data provenance concerns.
Why the reader benefits: Useful 2026 update showing privacy risk is not limited to classic membership inference.
Best use: Privacy section; training data; model memorization
Key ethical question: What does a model owe people whose private or copyrighted data it can reproduce?

Title: Spore: Efficient and Training-Free Privacy Extraction Attack on LLM Agent Memory
What it covers: Studies privacy leakage from inference-time contextual memory in LLM agents, beyond training-data privacy.
Why the reader benefits: Important for 2026 because persistent AI assistants and agents create a new privacy attack surface.
Best use: Agentic AI; memory privacy; security discussion
Key ethical question: What privacy risks appear when AI systems remember and act on user context over time?

Title: AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future
What it covers: Official overview of the EU AI Act, risk-based obligations, implementation timeline, GPAI rules and transparency requirements.
Why the reader benefits: Provides the clearest bridge between ethics principles and enforceable legal duties in 2026.
Best use: Regulation module; compliance discussion; policy comparison
Key ethical question: When should ethical expectations become legal obligations?
Notes / status: General application date: 2 August 2026, with exceptions and phased provisions.

Title: Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of AI systems
What it covers: Explains Article 50 duties concerning user disclosure, machine-readable marking, AI-generated content and deepfakes.
Why the reader benefits: Useful concrete example of how transparency ethics becomes a product-design requirement.
Key ethical question: Should people always know when they are interacting with AI or seeing AI-generated content?

Title: From Sycophancy to Deception: A Unified Taxonomy for Misleading LLM Behavior
What it covers: Unifies hallucination, omission, pragmatic distortion, sycophancy and strategic deception under a common taxonomy of misleading behavior.
Why the reader benefits: Helps readers avoid treating all misleading model outputs as the same failure mode.
Key ethical question: Does intent or goal-directedness change how ethically serious misleading AI behavior is?
